cluster_name: Supreme Court 5-4 allows Trump White House ballroom construction
tldr: Headlines across all 11 buckets converge on a single factual claim — the Supreme Court permitted ballroom construction — but split into two distinct registers: a neutral legal register (most international outlets frame it as the court 'clearing the way' or 'authorising') and an explicit Trump-victory register (conservative US, Italian, and Latin American papers frame it as a 'win', 'victory', or 'nueva victoria'). The Roberts dissent, prominent in body-text coverage internationally, is headline-visible only at The Independent; headline-only readers across 10 of 11 buckets receive no signal that a chief justice called the construction 'likely unlawful'.
event_summary: The U.S. Supreme Court voted 5-4 on August 31, 2026 to allow White House ballroom construction to continue, ruling the preservation group likely lacks standing without deciding the project's legality. Chief Justice Roberts dissented with the three liberals, calling construction 'likely unlawful.'

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only headline to foreground Roberts' 'likely unlawful' dissent rather than the court's permission to build, inverting the dominant frame used by all 20 other outlets; headline-only readers of every other outlet receive no signal that a chief justice opposed the ruling.

Only headline to editorialise against the project — 'Cumpla su capricho' (fulfill his whim) — framing the ruling as indulgence of a personal extravagance rather than a legal or institutional event; every other outlet, including the other Spanish-language papers, treats it as a factual ruling.

Only headline to include a cost figure (US$600m) as part of the lede, making the fiscal scale of the project visible to headline-only readers; all other non-US outlets omit cost entirely at headline level.
Only headline to bundle the ballroom ruling with a second story (Army secretary resignation), signalling to readers that SCOTUS is one of several concurrent stories rather than a standalone event.

bottom_line: At headline level, the Supreme Court ballroom ruling reads almost entirely as 'court permits construction' (LEGALITY), with conservative US, Italian, and Latin American outlets overlaying an explicit 'Trump wins' register (POLITICAL) — while the Roberts dissent that shapes international body coverage is invisible in 20 of 21 headlines.
